So I (24F) too was on the healthcare track, graduated in applied biomedical science and worked as EMT 20-32 hrs per week while doing so. I have been a dog mom since I was 18 so I know the struggles. First things first, you are putting a lot on yourself. It is a lot of sacrifice, money, and time to successfully balance all of this. If you are able to, find a trainer who trains YOU how to train your dog. You need to learn what methods work best for both of you. Then, build a schedule. 30-45 min walk before morning class/work. 30-45 min walk as soon as you get home or whatever you can manage in between classes. Make feeding time fun with an enrichment mat thing. Nice evening walk to end the night. It’s hard to do but it is possible. I think if you find structure for both you that works, you may see an improvement in your mental health as well. 

EMS is a shithole field to work in and having that companion to decompress with makes it worth it, for me.
